description: The image displays a set of three pie charts, labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard," which compare the proportions of four distinct categories across these three difficulty levels, with a general label "CoT" positioned below the center chart. Each of the three charts contains four slices. A shared legend on the right side of the image identifies the categories by color: a teal slice represents "N+K+", a yellow slice represents "N−K+", a light orange slice represents "N−K−", and a dark orange slice represents "N+K−". In the "easy" chart, the proportions are 45.9% for yellow (N−K+), 40.6% for teal (N+K+), 10.1% for light orange (N−K−), and 3.3% for dark orange (N+K−). The "medium" chart displays 44.6% for teal (N+K+), 44.3% for yellow (N−K+), 7.2% for light orange (N−K−), and 3.9% for dark orange (N+K−). Finally, the "hard" chart shows 36.8% for light orange (N−K−), 36.2% for yellow (N−K+), 20.1% for teal (N+K+), and 7.0% for dark orange (N+K−). All charts include numerical percentage labels directly inside their respective slices. There are no visually emphasized, exploded, or offset slices, and the segments are arranged in a consistent clockwise order (teal, yellow, light orange, dark orange) across all three charts rather than being strictly ordered by descending or ascending size.
